title: ARX Tier 1 Scorecard v2
historical: 68.7% was reported for PRs #21–#25 under an unavailable rubric. Not comparable to v2.
policy: Unweighted completion gates. PASS requires exact-commit review evidence and successful required checks. Missing or stale evidence is UNKNOWN. FAIL and UNKNOWN block required gates. DEFERRED is allowed only for explicit non-required rubric entries. No production access during measurement.

criteria.requirement: One deterministic authority evaluates risk; no independent permissive risk gate can bypass it.
Effective limits, sizing, conservative position counts and automated paper facts have canonical sources.
All supported order and management paths enforce the governor, including final broker dispatch.
Action-specific decisions preserve reasons, audit evidence, effective versus saved limits, and distinct operational caps.
Behavioral tests prove risk boundaries, halt enforcement, isolation and action-aware close permissions.
One execution authority owns common intent routing and lifecycle, with internal venue adapters.
Each command/book has one writer authority; automated paper records have one canonical book.
All supported producers and position operations enter the engine; no route writes execution mailboxes directly.
Modes, confirmation, retries, rejection, acknowledgement and execution are explicit; no silent LIVE-to-PAPER fallback.
Behavioral tests prove concurrent retry safety, ownership, broker refusal and real-quote paper fills and closes.
One management authority owns the six management rule families; pure rules cannot execute independently.
The position ledger owns access to both physical tables under approved Option A.
Position managers use Guardian rules and submit actions through the engine; runtime position persistence uses the ledger.
Named views distinguish exposure, unclosed, confirmed-open and alert eligibility with user/account/venue/ticket identity.
Behavioral tests prove management decisions, ledger isolation, position views and reconciliation without false execution.
Broker Hub supplies broker facts through read adapters and never authorizes or dispatches trades.
Connection, account snapshot and broker state readers provide scoped provenance; comparable heartbeat labels share one policy.
Runtime consumers use canonical readers and freshness definitions; necessary ingestion writes stay with their owner.
Capabilities and missing/stale facts remain truthful; stream health and account/position/quote freshness are distinct.
Behavioral tests prove adapter contracts, identity isolation, snapshot provenance and freshness boundaries.
One safety authority interprets stop switches, venue controls and their scope.
Switch readers and audited engage/release operations have canonical owners; duplicate rows cannot weaken stops.
Readiness and execution consume the same operator-control policy; new-risk controls are enforced at dispatch.
Activation never releases stops, resume never implicitly arms live, and recovery does not bypass action-specific policy.
Behavioral tests prove both stops, duplicate rows, release/activation, scope and execution/maintenance enforcement.
Library, API, dashboard and scripts typechecks pass.
All architecture guards pass without weakening or widening boundaries.
Relevant behavioral suites pass; every remaining integration failure is individually investigated with reproducible baseline evidence.
Owner evidence confirms all required migrations applied before deployment.
Owner inspection verifies broker controls and duplicate global settings.
A real market-data provider is configured and its provenance/freshness verified.
Legacy owner is explicit where ownerless rows must be claimed; no inferred ownership.
All seven broker validation scenarios pass on a real demo bridge.
Owner-controlled deployment and required alerting changes are verified.
Physical table consolidation, P0/D5/D6 and full-week cutover observation are future Option B prerequisites.
criteria.deferral: Owner decision 12 / D1–D10 selects Option A for this phase. Logical ledger authority remains required.
